albums.blurb: Recorded in Los Angeles over two days in December 1962 with Ray Brown on bass and Ed Thigpen on drums, Night Train catches Peterson's classic trio working through blues and R&B standards — Duke Ellington's title track, Milt Jackson's "Bags' Groove" — in deliberately short takes that producer Norman Granz hoped commercial radio would play. The closer, "Hymn to Freedom," is Peterson's best-known original composition and became an unofficial anthem of the civil rights movement after lyrics were later added.
albums.reception: The album won the jury-voted Polaris Heritage Prize in 2019, and The Penguin Guide to Jazz called it "one of the best-constructed long-players of the period."

albums.blurb: Frazer is the drummer and falsetto voice of Durand Jones & The Indications, and this is his debut solo album, released in January 2021 on Dead Oceans in partnership with Easy Eye Sound. Dan Auerbach of the Black Keys produced it in Nashville and co-wrote every song, setting Frazer's high, airy lead against late-'60s-styled sweet soul arrangements that reach into gospel and doo-wop.
albums.reception: American Songwriter rated the album 4 out of 5 stars and called it "one of the early contenders for finest debut of 2021."

albums.blurb: Little Dragon are a four-piece from Gothenburg, Sweden, built around singer Yukimi Nagano, whose guest turns on Gorillaz's Plastic Beach and SBTRKT's debut brought the band a wider audience around this time. Ritual Union is their third album, released on Peacefrog in 2011, and it tightens the futuristic soul of their first record and the synth-pop of Machine Dreams into spare, percussive electronic songs.
albums.reception: The album reached No. 22 on the UK Albums Chart and No. 78 on the Billboard 200, and Rolling Stone ranked it No. 41 on its 50 Best Albums of 2011 list.
